entities.summary:
Adrien Maurice de Noailles (1678-1766), 3rd Duke of Noailles and Marshal of France, stood as a pivotal military and political figure during the twilight of Louis XIV’s reign and the subsequent decades under Louis XV. His career, spanning nearly seven decades, saw him command French forces in major European conflicts, including the War of the Spanish Succession, the War of the Polish Succession, and the War of the Austrian Succession. A scion of one of France’s most ancient and powerful noble families, Noailles embodied the martial prowess and aristocratic influence that defined the French monarchy's global ambitions in the early modern period, playing a significant role in shaping French foreign policy and military strategy across the continent.

Noailles distinguished himself early, participating in the Siege of Barcelona in 1705 and later commanding French forces in Catalonia during the War of the Spanish Succession, where he captured Girona in 1711. Elevated to Marshal of France in 1734, he played a crucial role in the War of the Polish Succession, leading troops to victory in the Rhine campaigns. His command in the War of the Austrian Succession, particularly his involvement in the Battle of Dettingen in 1743, though not a decisive French victory, showcased his enduring strategic capabilities. Beyond the battlefield, Noailles served as President of the Council of Finance during the Regency (1715-1718), attempting to stabilize France's post-Louis XIV economy, and later as a Minister of State under Louis XV.
